title: Secondary palette
slide_intent: Teach when to expand the colors available for information or representation. A data category and a person’s skin tone call for different palette decisions.
strategic_value: Frontline AIDS can illustrate a range of people and explain complex data while a core color keeps the work connected to the identity.
demonstration: Supplementary hue swatches and skin-tone swatches occupy separate rows above a ring chart and a two-person illustration.
practical_value: Use secondary hues with at least one primary hue; keep the skin-tone range for character illustration.

content_islands.name: Extended colors
content_islands.spec: Use a grid of labeled color references for the secondary hues. Give the skin-tone range its own continuous row below.

content_islands.name: Data example
content_islands.spec: Show the chart with its palette chips and the note reserving skin tones for people.

content_islands.name: Character example
content_islands.spec: Place the two figures beside the chart with a separate note explaining the relationship between primary, secondary and skin-tone colors.
